<!--
Use a Conventional Commit PR title: <type>(<optional scope>): <description>

Examples:
  feat(incidents): add status filtering [ENG-123]
  fix(alerts): refresh details after selecting an alert [ENG-456]
  docs: clarify TUI configuration
  chore(deps): update dependencies

Use feat for new features, fix for bug fixes, and ! before the colon for
breaking changes, e.g. feat!: remove a deprecated configuration option.

Release Please uses commit messages for release notes and version bumps.
When squash-merging, ensure the final commit title follows this format too.
Keep relevant Linear issue IDs as a title suffix, as shown above, and link
the ticket in the description. The title must start with the Conventional
Commit type, not the ticket ID (e.g. avoid [ENG-123] feat(...): ...).
-->

## Description

<!-- What changes are being made, and why? Link related Linear issues here. -->

## Testing

<!-- Describe how the change was verified, or explain why tests are not needed. -->

## Risk Assessment

<!-- Describe potential impact, breaking changes, or migration steps. -->
